title: Night Chronicle: Incident Lens and Follow-ups (US-WEST GPU Latency Spike)
content:
Executive snapshot:
- Time window: 2026-03-22 00:42 - 2026-03-22 03:10 UTC (peak at ~01:05 UTC).
- Symptom: elevated p95/p99 latency on hosted-api inference pool (us-west-2, gpu-pool-g4dn), manifests as user-visible 500/504 and streaming stalls.
- Impact: ~8% of requests experienced >2s generation delay for 5–10 token responses; a small subset hit transient 5–10s stalls leading to client timeouts. No data loss, no privacy exposure.

Timeline (concise):
1) 00:42 UTC: paging alert - p99 > 1.8s for hosted-api/us-west-2 (alert: infra-high-latency). Pager duty -> on-call.
2) 00:47 UTC: quick triage, noticed concurrent driver package rollout (nvidia-driver 535.XX) started at 00:30 by release-engineering (tagged: REL-2026-03-22-driver).
3) 00:55 UTC: elevated GPU kernel errors observed in node logs (nvml warnings + repeated kernel timeouts) on 3 hosts.
4) 01:05 UTC: slowdowns cascade to fronting autoscaler causing queueing; we triggered emergency scaling and routed some traffic to fallback region (us-east-1).
5) 01:20 UTC: mitigations: rolled back driver on affected hosts to previous stable (534.YY). Latency returned to baseline over next ~15 minutes.
6) 02:00 UTC: monitoring stable; we kept additional capacity up for observation until 03:10 UTC.

Actions taken during shift (what we did):
- Immediate containment:
  - Identified driver rollout as probable cause from correlating release window + nvml kernel warnings (logs: /var/log/nvidia-drivers).
  - Scoped affected hosts using chef/labels and isolated them from autoscaler.
  - Rolled back driver package on 3 impacted nodes (patch id REL-2026-03-22-driver-rollback).
  - Manual traffic reroute added to route policy: route->fallback-region if model variant latency > 1.2s for 30s.
- Communication:
  - Notified Release Eng (Jared Morales) and GPU infra (Kenji) in Slack and opened JIRA-INC-4521.
  - Posted initial summary to #sre-ops and #platform-incidents.

Root cause assessment (working hypothesis):
- Primary hypothesis: recent driver binary (535.XX) contains a kernel-level regression when paired with our inference kernel selection for quantized Mamba-13B model; this causes occasional kernel stalls leading to NVML timeouts and OS-level scheduling delays.
- Evidence:
  - Temporal correlation: rollout start at 00:30, latency spike at 00:42.
  - Logs: repeated nvml/gpu kernel warnings on affected hosts, no similar errors on unaffected nodes that still had 534.YY.
  - Quick A/B: traffic shifted to nodes with old driver did not exhibit stalls.
- Unknowns:
  - Whether only specific GPU firmware + driver combo triggers the issue.
  - Whether model sequence length or attention kernel variant exacerbates it.

Follow-ups and ownership (short card list):
- SRE-128 (Kenji) - run controlled canary for nvidia-driver 535.XX with synthetic load and our exact inference workloads; include kernel tracing (deadline: 2026-03-25).
- RELEASE-PR-667 (Jared) - revert plan + add pre-rollout kernel smoke tests (owner: Jared Morales, deadline: 2026-03-24).
- RUNTIME-VAL-44 (Aisha) - add targeted e2e that runs Mamba-13B quantized path across driver matrix (owners: eng-serving-runtime + applied-ml, deadline: 2026-04-02).
- RUNBOOK update (SRE docs) - add a section for "GPU driver rollout rollback" with step-by-step: detect, isolate, rollback, validate (owner: Sofia Nguyen, draft due 2026-03-26).
- Observability delta - add NVML kernel warning as a dedicated alert (p95 count threshold) and tag correlated host IDs in traces (owner: Observability team, ticket OBS-303, target 2026-03-29).

Open tasks for incoming team (next on-call):
- Verify that all nodes in us-west-2 are on 534.YY and confirm no residual driver artifacts on OS (grep rpm, check dpkg depending on flavor).
- Validate that the autoscaler fallback routing has a cooldown and will not flip-flop; test with a synthetic ramp.
- Confirm with Release Eng whether drivers were provisioned via immutable images or package rollout; capture CI job IDs for that release.
- Attach kernel traces and the nvml log excerpts to JIRA-INC-4521 (I left raw logs in /tmp/sre-incident-INC-4521-logs.tgz).

Notes-to-self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider a small, always-on canary pool with pinned stable driver + telemetry to catch regressions before global rollout.
- Maybe add a preflight job that runs a short inference using the full quantized code-path on upgraded images.
- Recheck if this same driver version was rolled to dedicated clusters earlier this quarter (possible missed correlation).

Communications summary for postmortem (to include in P1 write-up):
- What happened: driver rollout -> rare kernel stalls -> backend queueing -> elevated user latency/timeouts.
- Impact: brief user-visible degraded latency for ~1–2 hours, contained with rollback and routing.
- Root cause: likely driver/kernel regression; investigations ongoing.
- Mitigations: rollback, traffic routing, increased capacity.
- Long-term fixes: canary policy, preflight tests, runbook additions, alert tuning.

Attachments / artifacts locations:
- Raw logs: /tmp/sre-incident-INC-4521-logs.tgz (on-call workstation)
- Grafana dashboards: linked above in linked_artifacts
- JIRA: JIRA-INC-4521, SRE-128
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/667

If you pick up the next window (thanks!):
- Read the JIRA thread first, then the nvml log excerpts.
- If anything reappears, immediately isolate nodes from LB and call Kenji / Jared (numbers in on-call roster).
- Otherwise, start the canary plan with Kenji and run a 2-hour synthetic workload with the new driver in a sandbox.

End note: rough draft for the postmortem is started in the INC ticket; will expand with kernel traces and timeline once SRE-128 completes the canary.

-- Aisha (overnight responder)
